football_evidence.question: Can Pittsburgh contain Georgia Tech’s explosive runs?
football_evidence.assessment: Some measured evidence supports EdgeDesk’s lean toward Pittsburgh, and its own breakdown accounts for about 0.1 of the 3.6 points, but not the full gap. It is a research question, not a bet.
supporting: When Pittsburgh has the ball (the line of scrimmage on running plays): Pittsburgh’s offense is stopped at or behind the line on 12.3% of its runs, and Georgia Tech’s defense stops 11.8% of opponent runs at or behind the line (FBS average 17.4%).

When Georgia Tech has the ball (the line of scrimmage on running plays): Georgia Tech’s offense is stopped at or behind the line on 18.2% of its runs, and Pittsburgh’s defense stops 24.2% of opponent runs at or behind the line (FBS average 17.4%).

When Pittsburgh has the ball (big plays on the ground): Pittsburgh’s offense turns 6.3% of its runs into explosive gains, and Georgia Tech’s defense gives up explosive gains on 9.6% of opponent runs (FBS average 6.5%).
When Georgia Tech has the ball (the run game against the run defense): Georgia Tech’s offense averages 5.5 yards per carry, and Pittsburgh’s defense allows 3.2 yards per carry (FBS average 5.1).
contradicting: When Georgia Tech has the ball (big plays on the ground): Georgia Tech’s offense turns 10.2% of its runs into explosive gains, and Pittsburgh’s defense gives up explosive gains on 5.2% of opponent runs (FBS average 6.5%).
In his last two games (North Carolina and Miami), Geriner averaged 6.4 yards per attempt, against 8.4 in his three games before that.
EdgeDesk’s position-group ratings put Georgia Tech’s running backs No. 21 nationally and Pittsburgh’s No. 69.

When Georgia Tech has the ball (the passing game against the pass defense): Georgia Tech’s offense averages 8.2 yards per pass attempt, and Pittsburgh’s defense allows 8.8 yards per pass attempt (FBS average 7.4).
quarterbacks: Mason Heintschel has completed 98 of 148 passes (66.2%) for 1,313 yards, 8.9 yards per attempt, 14 touchdowns and 1 interception in five games for Pittsburgh, and has been sacked on 5 of 153 dropbacks.
Holden Geriner has completed 64 of 102 passes (62.7%) for 706 yards, 6.9 yards per attempt, 3 touchdowns and 2 interceptions in five games for Pittsburgh, and has been sacked on 4 of 106 dropbacks.

Alberto Mendoza has completed 149 of 212 passes (70.3%) for 1,703 yards, 8.0 yards per attempt, 10 touchdowns and 6 interceptions in seven games for Georgia Tech, and has been sacked on 15 of 227 dropbacks.
